Roehampton Sports Ground Estate

Priory Lane and Bank Lane, London SW15 5JQ. Thirty-eight freehold acres owned by the Bank of England since 1908, home of the Wimbledon Qualifying Competition, offered as a whole or in four lots by Knight Frank. This brief sets out the estate, the income in place, BGP's commercial business plan and the working underwrite. The National Tennis Centre stays exactly as it is on the LTA's 125-year lease. The Grange residential conversion is left for Related to value.

The estate

Four lots, four different uses

Knight Frank invite offers for the whole, individual lots or combinations. The Bank reserves the right not to accept the highest offer, bids go in a prescribed format, and AML information is required at heads of terms. The site sits 500 m north of Richmond Park, with Barnes station 0.8 miles away.

The business plan

Three moves

Take a surrender of the All England Club's 2036 lease and regrant a 10-year lease of the grounds and the marquee rights for the Qualifying, remove the temporary pavilion, let the Sports Club and the whole Pavilion, 60,142 sq ft, to Third Space on a 20-year lease with the Squash Courts to follow if they want them, and hand The Grange to Related for a residential conversion. The cottages are sold or let with vacant possession. Lot 1 is not part of the plan: the National Tennis Centre remains the National Tennis Centre, the LTA keeps its lease to 2129 and no surrender or variation is proposed.

Move 1

Surrender and regrant with the All England Club

£100,000 pa

The Club surrenders its lease of the whole of Lot 2, which runs to 2036 with a 2031 break, and takes a new 10-year lease of the playing fields, the hard courts and the marquee rights already consented to 2031, with no building. The temporary pavilion at the north end of the Pavilion is removed. The Pavilion, sports hall, pool, squash courts and car parks come back to the landlord on the day of the surrender.

The Club's lease is outside the Act and runs to 2036, so the surrender has to be agreed, not imposed. Their lever is the 2031 break; ours is certainty of tenure for the Qualifying and a rent that falls from £350,000 to £100,000 for a smaller demise. Document the surrender and regrant as a condition of the purchase so the leisure buildings are vacant on completion.

Move 2

Let the Sports Club and the whole Pavilion to Third Space

£1.80m pa

The Sports Club and the whole permanent Pavilion, 60,142 sq ft GIA, with the 4,778 sq ft temporary pavilion, its link passage and porch removed first so the Pavilion is let as one building. A 20-year lease at £30 per sq ft GIA with two years rent free and a capital contribution equal to one year's rent. Rent indexed to CPI, reviewed five-yearly, capped at 3 percent a year. The Squash Courts, 3,233 sq ft, are a separate building and are excluded from the demise; the fenced 2G astro pitch beside the car park goes in, with a five-metre strip around it for seating and access, and the 162 parking bays come as rights rather than demise. Their own brief was about 50,000 sq ft, so the area is a live input in the underwrite below.

Splitting the leisure buildings

What Third Space take: the Sports Club and the whole Pavilion

Measured from the Principal Plans GIA drawings (September 2019). The Sports Club is the pool and sports hall building, 32,377 sq ft over four levels. The Pavilion is the 1920s clubhouse, 32,543 sq ft GIA as scheduled, of which 4,778 sq ft is the long-standing temporary pavilion at the north end of the building with its link passage and entrance porch, measured along its own thin-walled outline so the hall's south-west corner stays with the permanent building. The permanent building is 27,765 sq ft: an east block of changing rooms and offices nearest the Sports Club, a central section of bars and kitchens, and the main function hall with the first-floor lounge and roof terrace. The squash courts are a separate 3,233 sq ft building. Knight Frank's schedule gives the same totals: Sports Club 32,377 sq ft GIA (19,986 NIA) and Pavilion 32,543 sq ft GIA (21,157 NIA). The plan is to remove the temporary pavilion rather than split the Pavilion around it, let the Pavilion whole with the Sports Club, and decide the Squash Courts with Third Space. The Club keep the fields and the marquee rights and run the Qualifying from the consented marquees.

What the Club needs in Qualifying week.

Player and official facilities, hospitality, media and storage for a two-week event. In the plan they keep no building: the fields, the hard courts and the marquee and grandstand consents, and run the event from the consented marquees as the 2025 consent already allows for five years. Options A, B and B+ are the fallbacks if they insist on part of the Pavilion, at the cost of Third Space rent.

How the areas were measured.

The green GIA outlines were extracted from the Principal Plans PDFs and reproduce the schedule to within 0.1 sq m on every sheet. The temporary pavilion was measured off the Pavilion ground floor at the junction shown on the plan; the fallback options cut the Pavilion at the wall between the east block and the central bars. Knight Frank's building totals match. Principal Plans should confirm from the CAD before pricing, but these are measured figures, not estimates. The underwrite below uses 60,142 sq ft and can be changed.

Parking

Can the estate give Third Space 150 spaces and The Grange 30?

Yes on the marked bays that already exist. We traced every marked bay on the Warner Surveys topographic survey of August 2019, registering its ten sheets to the Ordnance Survey grid and then registering the Principal Plans building outlines onto them, and found 198 marked bays in two car parks against a requirement of 180. The main car park lies south of the Sports Club, wrapping the squash courts, between the club and Bank Lane; the smaller one sits at The Grange's north-east corner. The constraint is policy and the Club's new demise, not space: no new hardstanding on Metropolitan Open Land is needed.

Residents through the barrier, Third Space through the timber gates

Gate 1, the barrier, residential. The barrier-controlled entrance off Bank Lane beside the cottage, immediately south-west of The Grange. The drive runs up past the sub-station to The Grange's forecourt and the road along its west side, so residents reach their 36 bays without touching the main car park. Gate 2, the timber gates, Third Space. Forty metres further east along Bank Lane, a pair of timber gates opens straight into car park A. Today the car park runs one way, in at the barrier and out through these gates, which is where its painted EXIT arrows point; for Third Space the gates become the two-way entrance to their 162 bays and members walk up the road beside The Grange to the Sports Club's west door. Both gates exist and are in use, so swapping which traffic uses which is not development, provided neither is widened. The only other vehicle access to the estate is the Tennis Centre's own entrance off Priory Lane inside the LTA lease, which is not relied on.

Car park A and the Club's new lease.

Buying the whole estate makes this simple: both car parks are yours whichever lot the brochure puts them in. Car park A lies east of The Grange and south of the Sports Club, with the drive to Bank Lane, which is the land the brochure lot plan draws as The Grange's parking; today it sits inside the Club's demise and comes back on the surrender. The new lease must exclude it, and the Grange's 30 spaces and Third Space's 150 are then allocated by the landlord as above.

Policy.

Wandsworth is Inner London for London Plan standards. Priory Lane is low PTAL, where the residential maximum is around 0.5 spaces per home at PTAL 0 to 1 and 0.25 at PTAL 2 to 3. Thirty spaces for 50 to 70 homes is 0.4 to 0.6 per home, at or above the cap depending on PTAL. Under Class MA the spaces are existing and highways impact, not a parking ratio, is the test. Third Space's 150 is a tenant requirement, met from existing tarmac without any change of use of open land.

Underwrite

Commercial underwrite, three-year hold

Every figure in the left-hand panel is a BGP working assumption and can be changed. The model buys the whole estate in January 2027, sells the cottages, does the landlord's works in 2027, starts the Third Space lease in January 2028, takes the Club's surrender and regrants from 2028, and sells the commercial lots at the end of the hold on net initial yields with purchaser's costs deducted. The Grange is treated as sold to Related at £7m, Woody's figure; the headline then shows what the bid for the whole estate has to be for the target profit on cost, and clearing Related's number shows instead what the Grange would have to fetch at the purchase price entered. Debt is drawn against costs as they fall, interest is paid from income or equity, and the loan is repaid from sale proceeds.

Planning and risk

Buying without planning risk

The test for every part of the plan is that it works on existing consents, existing use classes and existing hardstanding, with nothing that needs a planning permission to make the numbers work. The table shows where each element stands. The one element that still needs a consent is The Grange conversion. Class MA prior approval is a 56-day, limited-test process, not a planning application, and the Bank is submitting it; the answer is sequencing, with the prior approval in hand before exchange or exchange conditional on it.

ElementPlanning positionStatusHow to keep it risk-free

Internal works are not development. The spa, sauna, creche and pool alterations were consented in 2007 and 2011 and are built.ExistingKeep the works inside the existing envelope. New external plant, flues or signage would need their own consents, so put them in the tenant's fit-out as tenant risk, not a landlord condition.
Removing the temporary pavilionTaking down a temporary structure is not a planning application. Demolition of a building over 50 cubic metres needs only the 28-day prior notification of the method of demolition and site restoration under Part 11, which the council cannot refuse on principle; the Bank ran the same process for the grounds structures in 2025 (2025/2066). The Grange: Class MA summary

What the residential permitted development route needs

The brochure says a detailed planning summary and the technical documents for the PD application are in the Knight Frank data room. They were not in the files we received, and the Wandsworth planning history runs only to the March 2026 lawful development certificate for the grounds building, so the application has not been registered. Ask Knight Frank for the PD pack. Against the Class MA tests as they stand after the March 2024 changes:

  • Class E use for two years before the application. Offices since at least 2017, when the ground floor South Wing changed from leisure to office. Met.
  • Vacancy. The three-month vacancy test was removed in 2024. The ITF leases end 31 December 2026 in any case.
  • Floorspace cap. The 1,500 sq m limit was removed in 2024, so the whole 5,361 sq m can convert.
  • Exclusions. Not listed, not in a Conservation Area, not a scheduled monument or safety hazard area. Metropolitan Open Land is not an exclusion from Class MA.
  • Prior approval matters. Transport and highways, contamination, flooding, noise from commercial neighbours, natural light to every habitable room, fire safety where the building is 18 m or more, and adequate space standards. The transport test is where the 30 existing spaces and the shared car park come in.
  • Grounds building and courts. Nothing in Class MA allows external works, so balconies, new openings or a roof extension would need a full application on MOL. Related's scheme should assume conversion within the envelope.
Risk register
High

The surrender itself. The Club's lease runs to 2036 outside the Act, so the surrender and regrant must be signed up before exchange, with the new lease excluding the leisure buildings and both car parks. Without it, Move 2 cannot start until 2031 or 2036.

High

Third Space covenant and terms. A 20-year lease on 60,142 sq ft at £30 GIA with three years of incentives is the whole commercial value, and is more space than the 50,000 sq ft they first asked for; the Squash Courts are the swing. Covenant strength, guarantor and the works specification need agreeing before the bid.

High

Grange prior approval. The conversion depends on Class MA prior approval, not yet applied for. Make it a condition of exchange or wait for the Bank's grant; the 56-day determination fits the timetable to a January 2027 completion.

Medium

Community campaign and Asset of Community Value. The Bank of England Centre Members' Group (saveboe.org) has campaigned since 2019 to keep the Sports Centre and pool for the community, with MPs Fleur Anderson and Sarah Olney and Sport England drawn in over the pool. Wandsworth's register shows the playing fields (football, rugby, cricket and the artificial pitch, not the buildings) listed as an Asset of Community Value on 1 August 2019 on a Roehampton and Putney Heath nomination; the Bank gave notice of disposal that September, the community moratorium ran to March 2020 and the listing expired in 2024. A fresh nomination can be made at any time and would put a six-month moratorium on the sale, so check the register at exchange. Expect the Third Space plan to be judged locally on whether the pool and hall stay open to local members, which is also the Club's interest.

Medium

Parking. 198 marked bays traced from the 2019 survey against 180 needed. Car park A sits inside the Club's demise today, so the new lease must exclude it; car park B is The Grange's own.

Medium

Holding cost of The Grange. Around £1m a year empty from January 2027 until Related take it.

Medium

Guarantor on the Tennis Centre lease. Due diligence only; the LTA lease is not being touched. The 2011 deed substituted LTA CLG Ltd for the All England Club. Confirm the brochure's "Lawn Tennis Association Limited" is the same entity, and that nothing has changed since.

Low

Title. Rent-charges of £57 from a 1779 deed on titles 239100 and 396768; Registrar's restrictions against charges on the older titles; a 1997 sub-station lease and 2009 EDF transformer lease; a right of way over part of Clarence House. Nothing seen that blocks the plan.

Low

VAT. Brochure says The Grange is opted to tax; Gerald Eve's 2025 budget says the landlord has not waived exemption. Reconcile before structuring.

Note

Environmental. Groundsure Siteguard (September 2019) concluded acceptable environmental risk for banking security; Part 2A or third-party action unlikely.
